title: First thing today
instructions: Ask about their morning. Accept any answer warmly. Draw out more detail.
script: What's the first thing you did when you got up today?
Ask how that specific action made them feel
Connect it to their routine - is this typical or different?

title: Weather check
goal: Connect to present moment through environment
instructions: Ask about weather and how it affects them. Keep it conversational.
script: What's the weather like where you are today?
Ask how this specific weather affects their mood or plans
Explore a memory or preference related to the weather they mentioned

title: Comfort spot
instructions: Ask about where they're sitting. Help them appreciate their space.
script: Are you in your usual spot today, or somewhere different?
Ask what they specifically like about that spot
Explore what makes it comfortable or meaningful to them

title: Time of day
instructions: Ask about their sense of the day. Accept approximate answers.
script: Is it morning, afternoon, or evening where you are?
Ask how this time of day typically feels for them
Explore what they enjoy doing at this time

title: Window view
instructions: Ask what they see. Draw out sensory details.
script: If you look out a window or around the room, what do you notice?
Ask about the specific thing they mentioned - color, shape, or feeling it gives
Connect what they see to a memory or association

title: Plans today
instructions: Ask about plans. Help them look forward to something.
script: Do you have any plans for today, or is it a relaxed day?
Ask what part of their plan (or relaxation) they're most looking forward to
Explore who might be involved or what makes it meaningful

title: Sleep check
instructions: Ask about sleep. Be supportive whatever they share.
script: How did you sleep last night?
Ask about dreams or what helped/hindered their sleep
Explore their sleep routine or what helps them rest

title: Something different
instructions: Ask about anything unusual. Help them reflect on their day.
script: Is there anything different about today compared to yesterday?
Ask how that difference makes them feel
Explore whether they prefer routine or variety

title: Favorite thing
instructions: Ask them to describe something they like. Encourage detail.
script: What's something in your home that you really like? Can you describe it to me?
Ask about a specific detail they mentioned - why that matters to them
Explore where it came from or how long they've had it

title: Finish the thought
instructions: Offer a sentence starter. Explore their answer.
script: Let me give you a sentence to finish: 'The best part of my week is...'
Ask why that specific thing brings them joy
Explore if it's something they look forward to regularly

title: Would you rather
instructions: Offer two options. Explore their reasoning.
script: Quick question: would you rather have coffee with an old friend, or take a quiet walk alone?
Ask what specifically appeals to them about their choice
Explore a recent time they got to do something like that

title: Word association
instructions: Say a word, ask what comes to mind. Explore the connection.
script: I'll say a word, and you tell me the first thing that comes to mind. Ready? The word is 'home.'
Ask why that specific thing came to mind
Explore the memory or feeling connected to their association

title: A photo you love
instructions: Ask about a photo or picture. Draw out the story.
script: Is there a photo or picture that means a lot to you? What's in it?
Ask about a specific person or detail they mentioned
Explore the feeling or memory that photo captures

title: Morning or night person
instructions: Ask about preference. Explore why.
script: Are you more of a morning person or a night person?
Ask what they specifically enjoy about that time
Explore if this has changed over their life

title: Favorite season
instructions: Ask about seasons. Explore memories connected to it.
script: What's your favorite season of the year?
Ask what they specifically love about that season
Explore a favorite memory from that season

title: Advice you'd give
instructions: Ask for advice. Explore the story behind it.
script: If someone asked you for one piece of advice about life, what would you tell them?
Ask where they learned that lesson
Explore a time when that advice helped them

title: Breakfast recall
instructions: Ask about food today. Explore preferences.
script: What did you have to eat this morning?
Ask if that's a usual choice or something different
Explore their favorite breakfast or who taught them to make it

title: A song you love
instructions: Ask about a song. Explore when they first heard it.
script: Is there a song that always makes you feel good when you hear it?
Ask when they first heard that song or what it reminds them of
Explore the person, place, or time connected to that song

title: Smell memory
instructions: Ask about a smell that triggers memory. Explore the scene.
script: Is there a smell that takes you back to a certain time or place?
Ask about the specific place or time that smell brings back
Explore who was there or what was happening

title: Childhood game
instructions: Ask about games or play. Explore the people involved.
script: What's a game you used to play when you were young?
Ask who they played it with
Explore where they played or a specific time they remember

title: Favorite meal
instructions: Ask about a favorite meal. Explore the story.
script: What's a meal that always makes you feel good?
Ask who used to make it or where they had it
Explore what makes that meal special or comforting

title: Recent conversation
instructions: Ask about recent communication. Explore the relationship.
script: Have you talked to anyone on the phone or had a visitor lately?
Ask what they talked about with that person
Explore how it felt to connect with them

title: A place you loved
instructions: Ask about a place. Explore sensory details.
script: Is there a place you've been that you really loved?
Ask what they remember seeing, hearing, or feeling there
Explore who they were with or what they did there

title: A teacher or mentor
instructions: Ask about someone who taught them. Explore the impact.
script: Was there a teacher or mentor who made a difference in your life?
Ask what specifically they taught or showed them
Explore how that person's influence shaped them

title: Holiday memory
instructions: Ask about a holiday. Explore traditions.
script: Is there a holiday that brings back good memories for you?
Ask about a specific tradition or moment from that holiday
Explore who was usually there and what made it special

title: First job
instructions: Ask about work. Explore what they learned.
script: What was one of your first jobs or responsibilities?
Ask what they learned from that experience
Explore a person who helped them or a moment they remember

title: Sounds around you
instructions: Ask about sounds. Explore what they notice.
script: Pause for a moment. What sounds do you hear around you right now?
Ask about the specific sound they mentioned - what it might be
Explore if any sound is comforting or familiar to them

title: Name three
instructions: Ask for 3 items. Accept any number. Celebrate effort.
script: Can you name three things that are blue?
Ask which of those they like best and why
Explore a memory or association with one of their answers

title: Counting down
instructions: Ask to count backward. Make it playful.
script: Let's do a quick focus exercise. Can you count backward from 10 to 1?
Ask how that felt - easy, challenging, fun?
Explore if they use counting or focus tricks in daily life

title: What's nearby
instructions: Ask them to notice objects. Explore what they see.
script: Without moving, what's one object you can see within arm's reach?
Ask about the specific object - color, texture, or meaning
Explore how they got it or how long they've had it

title: Animals that...
instructions: Ask for animals. Explore favorites.
script: Can you name a few animals that live in water?
Ask which of those animals they find most interesting and why
Explore if they've ever seen one in real life

title: Deep breath
instructions: Guide a breath. Check in on how it felt.
script: Let's take a deep breath together. Breathe in slowly... and out.
Ask how that felt in their body
Explore if they have ways to relax or find calm

title: Rhyming words
instructions: Ask for rhymes. Make it playful.
script: Can you think of a word that rhymes with 'day'?
Celebrate their word and ask for another rhyme
Explore if they ever made up rhymes, songs, or poems

title: Opposite game
instructions: Ask for opposites. Keep it fun.
script: Let's play a quick game. What's the opposite of 'hot'?
Celebrate and give another opposite to find
Ask one more opposite - make it playful

title: Someone kind
instructions: Ask about a kind person. Explore what they did.
script: Is there someone who was especially kind to you at some point in your life?
Ask what specifically that person did that stayed with them
Explore how that kindness affected them or shaped who they are

title: Something you're proud of
instructions: Ask about accomplishment. Celebrate their effort.
script: What's something you've done in your life that you're proud of?
Ask what it took to accomplish that - the effort or challenges
Explore how they felt when they achieved it

title: Family tradition
instructions: Ask about traditions. Explore the people involved.
script: Did your family have any traditions or rituals you remember?
Ask what made that specific tradition special to them
Explore who started it or kept it going

title: Lesson learned
instructions: Ask about a lesson. Explore the story.
script: What's something life has taught you that you wish you'd known earlier?
Ask how they learned that lesson - what happened
Explore if they've been able to pass it on to someone

title: Favorite age
instructions: Ask about a favorite time. Explore what made it good.
script: If you could go back to any age, which would you choose?
Ask what specifically was good about that time in their life
Explore what they would want to bring from that age to today

title: A best friend
instructions: Ask about a friend. Explore shared experiences.
script: Who was a good friend to you over the years?
Ask what they used to do together with that friend
Explore what made their friendship work

title: Something brave
instructions: Ask about bravery. Explore what helped.
script: Was there a time when you did something that took courage?
Ask what the hardest part of that situation was
Explore what helped them get through it

title: Someone you think of
instructions: Ask about someone on their mind. Explore the relationship.
script: Is there someone you've been thinking about lately?
Ask what comes to mind when they think of that person
Explore what they would want to say to them

title: One word
instructions: Ask for one word. Acknowledge and close warmly.
script: If you had to pick one word to describe how you feel right now, what would it be?
Reflect their word back and ask what made them choose it
Warmly close the session, referencing something they shared

title: Carry a thought
goal: Send user off with positive anchor
instructions: Reference something they shared. End with warmth.
script: Before we go, I want you to know: you showed up today, and that matters.
Ask what one thing from the conversation they might carry with them
Close warmly, referencing their answer

title: Until next time
instructions: End with warmth and a gentle hook.
script: I really enjoyed talking with you today.
Ask if there's anything they'd like to talk about next time
Close warmly with anticipation for next session

title: Best part of today
instructions: Ask about something good. Celebrate it.
script: What's been the best part of your day so far?
Ask what made that moment stand out for them
Close warmly, wishing them more moments like that

title: Grateful for today
instructions: Ask about gratitude. Accept any answer.
script: Is there anything you feel grateful for today?
Ask what specifically they appreciate about that thing
Close warmly, thanking them for sharing

title: Hope for tomorrow
instructions: Ask about tomorrow. Support their hope.
script: Is there anything you're looking forward to tomorrow?
Ask what would make tomorrow a good day for them
Close warmly with hope for their tomorrow

title: Be kind to yourself
instructions: Offer gentle closing with reflection.
script: Before we finish, remember to be kind to yourself today.
Ask what one small way they might do that
Close warmly, affirming they're doing just fine

title: Enjoyed your company
instructions: Thank them sincerely. End warmly.
script: I really enjoyed your company today.
Ask what their favorite part of the conversation was
Close warmly, referencing what they shared
